criteria.notes: What this box does and does not evidence. It evidences the FAKE's agreement with hand-derived expectations — which is exactly what the criterion says. It does not evidence the real engine's agreement with the fake; the phase's own final Risks bullet reserves that for 06's @live suite, and this pass ran no live test. Engine-fact check (README ground rule 5): docs/engine-baseline.md §14.4 (2026-08-01) supersedes §14.3 and records that a path-scoped rule is honored as an ALLOW rule and was not honored as a DENY rule. None of the seven fixtures depends on a path-scoped deny firing: the two path-escape fixtures deny because NO allow rule matches (default-deny under dontAsk, which §14.4 explicitly reaffirms as the mechanism that actually contains a worker), the deny-wins pair uses Bash command-prefix rules citing §3's live probes, and the blanket-mcp-deny fixture is a tool-name pattern outside §14.4's Write-tool path-rule scope. Two documented fidelity limits carried from the phase's own evidence README, so the tick is not read wider: the sandbox evaluator deliberately does not check filesystem.allowWrite (placeholder tokens only until 06/07 substitute real paths), which is why both path-escape fixtures record sandbox: 'allow'; and path-matching.ts's cross-anchor handling is hardened but not complete (documented as a known limitation that can only over-deny, never over-allow).
